author: agent:claude-code
message: First design of sylva, adopted from what the code already is: three layers (structures, log, knowledge) as in docs/DESIGN.md, each component linked to its code, with the rules, checks and decisions the design document states. (proposal 01a10a55-0008-766e-82ef-2e5ea503f78a, proposed by agent:claude-code, accepted by user)

text: Determinism: the same ops give the same state, byte for byte, on every machine; iteration follows key order, never insertion order or slot layout.
Pure Rust; SQLite is the one native dependency, optional and bundled, so the crate builds for desktop, server and iOS.
No graph database, query language, general collection library or algorithm catalogue: only the walks and queries Sylva's users need.

name: Foundation
intent: The Key trait and the Error type every layer shares.

name: Structures
intent: General-purpose graphs and trees with stable keys, dense storage and the indexes real queries need, iterating in key order.

text: Neighbours and degrees cost the node's degree, not the graph; paths, ancestors and subtree walks are iterators that don't allocate per step.
Equality compares content, never storage layout.

name: Graph
intent: A directed graph generic over node and edge data: adjacency both ways sorted by edge key, walks, shortest paths and topological order.

name: Tree
intent: An ordered forest: lineage, ancestors, pruned subtree and preorder walks, and moves that refuse cycles.

name: Log
intent: Makes any state remember: changes are ops in batches, state is the replay of the log, branches merge, and any past step can be rebuilt (feature `log`).

name: Batches
intent: Batches with their header, the canonical JSONL form, causal order, projections and a replay that keeps ops that no longer apply as conflicts.

text: Replay never fails: an op that doesn't apply becomes a Conflict for a person to resolve.
Causal order is the same for any set of batches in any input order.

name: History
intent: Keeps a projection's replayed state current, applying a batch that follows the head alone, with snapshots for time travel.

name: Batch files
intent: One file per batch, so two branches never edit the same file.

name: Hash chain
intent: One writer's ops in sequence, each sealing the previous hash, so any edit to the past is detected.

text: The hash encoding ({seq, id, batch, parent, ts, actor, op} as JSON in that order) is pinned by a test: every existing chain depends on it.

name: Signatures
intent: Ed25519 signatures over a batch's canonical form under a caller-chosen domain, verified against trusted keys (feature `sign`).

name: SQLite store
intent: The hash chain stored in SQLite, one row per op, with payloads run through a codec (feature `sqlite`).

name: Encryption at rest
intent: A codec that seals each stored op with XChaCha20-Poly1305 under a data key derived per application from one master key (feature `crypt`).

text: The stored format (`e1:` + base64(nonce || ciphertext), the op's hash as associated data) is Alfred's byte for byte; rows without the prefix read as plain JSON.

name: Knowledge
intent: A typed property graph and a catalog tree built from ops on the structures: schemas, stated vs observed facts, references, queries and diagrams (feature `knowledge`), with TypeScript types generated by ts-rs (feature `ts`) that match its written-out JSON.

text: Op JSON is stored data (Alfred's log and every repo's .tend/log): field names, tags and enum spellings change only with a migration.
An op that would change nothing is rejected.

name: References
intent: References to entities owned elsewhere (`domain/kind/id`, `files:path`, a host's `scheme:path`), validated in shape.

name: Attributes
intent: Typed attribute definitions and the check of a value against one.

name: Catalog trees
intent: Catalog trees whose nodes are retired, split, merged and restored rather than deleted, with attributes their descendants inherit.

name: Property graphs
intent: Property graphs with schemas and facts that record where they came from, plus queries, a name-based change language and Mermaid, DOT and D2 rendering.

text: An observation never overwrites or removes what was stated.

check.name: unit tests
check.notes: Unit tests live next to each module.

title: One crate with features, not five
body: Splits only pay where consumers need different dependencies; features handle that.

title: No separate signing crate
body: Signing is a property of batches; key custody belongs to the application.

title: Ordered BTreeMap index, not a hash map
body: Deterministic iteration with no extra sorting, and no hasher dependency.

title: Adjacency sorted by edge key
body: Same order as a scan of all edges by key, so results didn't change when the scan went away.

title: Conflicts as data, not errors
body: Merged histories must always replay; people resolve what doesn't apply.

title: The caller picks the signature domain
body: One key can't be tricked into signing for another purpose. Tend's domain stays `alfred-tend-batch-v1\n` so existing signatures remain valid.

title: Encryption keys derived per application
body: One master key can serve several apps (HMAC-SHA256 of `<app>/v1/data`) without any two sharing a data key.

title: Extracted from Alfred
body: Sylva was extracted from Alfred so Alfred and Tend build on one implementation; its bar is Alfred's benchmark baseline (alfred/docs/benchmarks/baseline.md), checked by benchmarks rather than assumed.

title: Move Alfred's store onto crypt and drop its own copy of the cipher
Serde for the generic Graph and Tree, for users without the knowledge model
A reverse-relation index pattern for projections that ask what points at this

text: Foundation doesn't use Structures, Log or Knowledge: they build on it.
Structures don't use Log or Knowledge and don't import serde_json: they stay general-purpose (serde derives behind the `serde` feature are fine).
